from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

# This is our playbook. The skeleton of the operation.
# We define the flow here so the team knows the sequence of play.
class SortAlgorithm(ABC):
    def sort(self, data):
        """The Template Method: Defines the overall structure of the drill."""
        n = len(data)
        # We're running a nested loop structure here—standard formation.
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(0, n - i - 1):
                if self.compare(data[j], data[j + 1]):
                    self.swap(data, j, j + 1)
        return data

    @abstractmethod
    def compare(self, element1, element2):
        """Subclasses decide the specific criteria for the comparison."""
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def swap(self, data, index1, index2):
        """Subclasses handle the actual movement of the players."""
        pass

# Strategy 1: The Bubble Sort Drill
# We're pushing the heavy hitters to the back of the line.
class BubbleSort(SortAlgorithm):
    def compare(self, element1, element2):
        # Standard ascending order—keep it simple, keep it clean.
        return element1 > element2

    def swap(self, data, index1, index2):
        data[index1], data[index2] = data[index2], data[index1]

# Strategy 2: The Selection Sort Drill
# We're scouting the field for the best position and moving them in.
class SelectionSort(SortAlgorithm):
    def sort(self, data):
        """Overriding the skeleton because Selection Sort needs a different formation."""
        n = len(data)
        for i in range(n):
            min_idx = i
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                if self.compare(data[j], data[min_idx]):
                    min_idx = j
            self.swap(data, i, min_idx)
        return data

    def compare(self, element1, element2):
        # Looking for the smallest value to bring to the front.
        return element1 < element2

    def swap(self, data, index1, index2):
        data[index1], data[index2] = data[index2], data[index1]
